scope: Read-only review of entry freeze-v4: one provider-proxy journaling change; offline fake-writer E2E; opt-in native/default-approval/checkpoint E2E; generated inventory/build metadata. No GUI, test execution, rebuild, source modification or commit during this review. Only this report written.

runtimeAssessment.conclusion: No unresolved production blocker found for supported caller contexts. The normal provider/agent loop passes ctx.session plus authoritative ctx.sessionId/turnSeq; the selected live session now reaches the path guard and journal with that same ctx before callTool. CLI/MCP calls pass null ctx and retain the loaded WCW_SESSION_ID/turnSeq fallback. Unscoped calls still skip journaling gracefully.
callerChecks: Provider/workflow supplies sessionId, turnSeq, session, config, workingDir and signal
Agent loop supplies the same session and turn fields
HTTP sessionId path loads its session before dispatch
MCP child null-context fallback retains the prior loaded-session construction
preservedGuards: Tool/catalog policy, tiers, required args, Office gate and absolute write-path refusal remain before dispatch
Bridged read path gate remains before journal and actual MCP call
Journal remains best-effort, per-target and before the actual bridge call
runtimeAssessment.contextLimit: Review does not establish a new public contract for arbitrary inconsistent/session-only ctx objects. Known production callers use coherent session and id/turn fields; journalSessionCtx prioritizes explicit ctx id/turn.

testAssessment.offline: Real service/session/provider turn/proxy/fake-MCP file writer, four unique create/overwrite cases. The matching turn_summary, exact fake bytes, before-image bytes and rollback state make the original missing-context defect observable. Image encoding/native capture are deliberately outside this offline fixture.
testAssessment.native: Only provider replies are fake. Uses real owned receiver, actual ACC/native helper, ordinary default-mode permission requests and decision/cancel endpoints. Allow is coupled to receiver counts and enclosing/native audit; deny/cancel require no receiver/audit mutations and no pending permission. Four image cases verify actual PNG, changed overwritten bytes, correct session/turn checkpoint and exact rollback.
testAssessment.isolation: Both use self-isolate-home/fixtureChildEnv and own data/work directories. Native HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA are explicitly isolated; process.env precedes the same isolated env overrides, so the inventory-friendly expression does not weaken isolation. Background imports/scheduler/steward/MCP autodetection are disabled.
testAssessment.desktopCleanup: Native fixture snapshots the clipboard before seeding controlled image formats, restores conditionally by ownership version, and records source-abc/original-source restoration. No Cmd+V or original clipboard payload is used by the test actions. Native workers receive owned SIGTERM before tree cleanup; final clipboard/input-source success is required if those states were touched.
testAssessment.processCleanupScope: Observed owned birth identities only, not a census of arbitrary unobserved escaped processes. Incomplete/skipped receipts fail the fixture and preserve its isolated root. No actual cleanup or failure injection was executed by this reviewer.

basis: Node24 built-ins only; process.execPath and argument arrays, no shell syntax

windowsAssessment.limits: No same-SHA Windows runtime result is claimed. Existing checkpoint-mcpchild covers native CLI file_write and tool-loading covers proxy/catalog paths; neither alone proves every CLI bridged-write journal branch. The null-ctx fallback compatibility conclusion here is source-based.

findings.title: Bind native checkpoint to the actual turn
findings.issue: The original assertion accepted any finite turnSeq in the right session, so a wrong-turn entry could be rolled back and mislabelled as per-turn evidence.
findings.resolution: Requires a positive integer and equality to this turn's turn_summary.turnSeq.

findings.title: Do not equate root exit with complete owned cleanup
findings.issue: Both fixtures ignored killOwnTree incomplete/skipped results and only awaited the root. The cleanup helper explicitly supports degraded direct-child cleanup; this was an evidence gap, not an observed leak.
findings.resolution: Snapshots root/descendant birth identities before cleanup, preserves receipts, rejects incomplete/skipped, confirms observed identities gone and retains isolated data on failure. Native worker graceful stop precedes force cleanup; receiver identity exit is separately verified. BigInt creation stamps serialize as strings.

findings.title: Prove fake overwrite mutation actually occurred
findings.issue: A pre-existing overwrite target plus any non-error result did not prove this fake writer changed the bytes.
findings.resolution: Correlates call_image and requires complete FAKE_WINDOW_PNG or FAKE_CLIP_PNG bytes; before-image and exact rollback checks remain.

findings.issue: README total advanced from588 to590 while the default count remained581. With seven configured runner exclusions, the current default candidate count is583.
findings.resolution: Both README default counts are583, total590; no test assertions removed.
